Part 1 · Using assumption 2
Why Σvx² = Σv² / 3
x
y
z
Particle 1
v₁² = vx₁² + vy₁² + vz₁²
Particle 2
v₂² = vx₂² + vy₂² + vz₂²
Add all
Σvᵢ² = Σvxᵢ² + Σvyᵢ² + Σvzᵢ²
Symmetry
Σvxᵢ² = Σvyᵢ² = Σvzᵢ²
So
Σvᵢ² = 3 Σvxᵢ²
Therefore
Σvxᵢ² = Σvᵢ² / 3
Careful: one particle need not have vx = vy = vz. Only the sums are equal.

Part 2 · One collision
Change in momentum in one collision
+vx
−vx
before: +mvx
after: −mvx
The particle bounces back elastically: vx → −vx. Only the x-momentum changes.
Δp = (−mvx) − (+mvx)
Magnitude:
Δp = 2mvx

Part 3 · Kinetic energy
Total kinetic energy of the gas
Add all
KE = ½mv₁² + ½mv₂² + … + ½mvN²
Factor
KE = ½ m Σvᵢ²
Use RMS
KE = ½ m N v²ᵣₘₛ
Total mass
mN = M = total mass of the gas
KE = ½ M v²ᵣₘₛ

using PV = nRT
NINE EDUCATION · Pressure of an Ideal Gas · Part 03 · Kinetic energy
20
Part 3 · Potential energy
PE = 0 for an ideal gas
no force between particles
ideal gas
Careful: (3/2) nRT is the translational KE. For a monoatomic gas it is the whole internal energy.
PE = 0
There is no interaction between the particles.
So all the energy of an ideal gas is kinetic:
KE = (3/2) nRT
⇒
KE ∝ T

4
PE = 0
No interaction between the particles of an ideal gas.
5
KE ∝ T
Higher temperature, more kinetic energy.
